transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Drowned Priest [T-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the plank walkways of Hollowmoot, and the quarantine bell has not stopped its tired, wet clang since noon. Lanterns gutter under sagging eaves as the crowd in the market square press close around a woman soaked to the bone, her shawl plastered to her shoulders, mud to her knees from wading the last stretch of causeway. She catches sight of you—strangers, capable-looking, still dry enough to have somewhere better to be—and shoves through the press of bodies to grab at sleeves and coat-hems. "My boy," she says, voice cracking, "he heard the singing from the belltower. Saint Orrin's. He's not right anymore, I know he's not, but he's still mine. Please. The water's rising, it'll take the ford by morning tide, and after that—" She doesn't finish. Behind her, someone mutters the word "hive-touched" like a curse, and a Warden at the watchtower rail is already watching the four of you a little too closely.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your boy's still yours, no matter what took him—I've seen enough good people twisted by this blight to know the difference between corruption and the soul underneath. We'll help you find him, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde reaches out and steadies the soaked woman with a firm hand on her shoulder, meeting her eyes with the quiet certainty of someone who knows what it means to be cast out. She can feel the Warden's gaze burning into her back, but she doesn't look away from Tessa's face. Some things are worth the risk of being seen.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Your boy heard singing from the belltower—that's not madness, that's the hive marking one of its own. We have until dawn tide swallows the ford. Tell me everything about him, *now*.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous shoulders through the market throng toward the woman, rain streaming off his cloak like scripture. He reads the downpour in real time—the water is rising with *purpose*, speaking in tongues only he can decipher. His eyes lock onto Tessa, and he plants himself squarely before her, ignoring the Warden's weight of attention at the rail. The drowned dead cling to him always; they always *know* when a soul is slipping away.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I know what "not right" means, and I know you're not cursed for loving him anyway. Tell me quickly—what's your boy's name, and when did he hear the singing?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen gently but firmly takes Tessa's shoulders, meeting her eyes with the steady confidence of someone who has faced the hive before and lived. She doesn't flinch at the word "hive-touched"—her whole life has been shaped by the first outbreak—and she tilts her body slightly to shield the conversation from the Warden's gaze, drawing Tessa close like someone bringing bad news to the kitchen table. Her voice is low, practical, but not cold: the voice of someone who has learned when hope is possible and when it isn't.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I know that look—I wore the grey too. We'll find your boy before the water takes the ford.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves through the press of bodies with the steady authority of someone trained to command, stepping into Tessa's reach. She meets the soaked woman's eyes without flinching, even as she feels the Warden's gaze from the watchtower rake across her back. Her jaw sets, and she puts a calloused hand on Tessa's shoulder—a grip that says this isn't negotiable. She'll hold this line, whether the wardens like it or not.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Tessa, listen to me—I'm known here, and that Warden knows my face. Stay close to the others and don't panic. Let me handle this.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Notice: dice - - - 0, invoking Fortune-Teller Who Reads the Rain, Sole Survivor of the Wreck [AL-HC] → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous doesn't wait for an invitation. He plants himself in front of Tessa and reads the rain the way other men read a ledger—the slant of it, the color of the runoff sluicing off the eaves, the particular urgency in how it's falling. "The ford holds till first light, maybe less," he says, flat and certain. "After that it's gone till low tide finds it again, and low tide won't come soon enough to matter." Tessa's breath catches; she gives them the boy's name—Corin—and says he slipped out three nights back, drawn toward the belltower like a man walking in his sleep. But Morwen's attempt to keep this quiet fails her: the Warden at the tower rail has already placed her face, and there's no unseeing a name like hers in a crowd this size. "That's the Exorcist," someone hisses, and heads turn. The Warden starts down the ladder toward the square, hand resting meaningfully on the truncheon at his belt, and the quarantine bell gives one more tired clang as if in answer.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Warden, you see what we see—the blight, the water, the time bleeding away. We're not spreading sickness. We're here to find the boy before he's lost entirely, and before the ford drowns him with us.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward to meet the Warden as he descends, placing herself calmly between him and the rest of the group. Her hands are open, her posture unthreatening but steady—the stance of someone who has faced down her own fears and knows how to meet another person's with clarity. She reads the weight on his shoulders: duty, fear, exhaustion in equal measure. She'll speak to that.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Get out of our way, Warden. That boy's still salvageable, and the flood won't wait for your authority.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps directly into the Warden's path, shoulders squared against the downpour, and the drowned dead press close against his shadow—the Warden will feel it if he's got any sense. His eyes are hollow and certain, the eyes of a man who has already looked into the dark beneath the flood and come back marked. He reaches back for Tessa's arm and starts moving through the crowd toward the belltower, not running, not breaking stride. Just walking. Like a man certain that no Causeway Warden will dare stop him.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Warden, I know what you're trying to protect—and so am I. That boy needs an exorcist, not torches. Give me till dawn tide. You know my work here.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward to meet the Warden before he can close the distance to Tessa, her shoulders squared and her eyes steady. She doesn't defer or retreat, but her voice carries respect—she knows he's trying to protect the city same as she is. She invokes her work as a known exorcist, her long connection to Hollowmoot's pilgrim band, and the simple truth that a boy hive-touched needs an exorcist far more than he needs a pyre. She's not begging permission; she's establishing why she belongs here and why this work matters.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I've still got business with this woman, Warden. Stand down.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves with trained efficiency, positioning herself directly between the descending Warden and Tessa. She mirrors his stance, hand resting on her belt, meeting his eyes with the quiet certainty of someone who knows exactly what it means to wear grey—and what it means to be cast out. She hasn't forgotten how to hold a line, disgraced or not.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: You want to test me, grey coat? I still remember the drills. I still remember how to hold.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Empathy: dice - - 0 -, invoking Exiled Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything [YS-HC] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Rapport: dice - 0 - +, invoking Exorcist Who Doubts the Hive Has Souls [MO-HC] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Provoke: dice + - 0 +, invoking Disgraced Warden Who Still Holds the Line on Wick Lane [MI-HC] → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The Warden's boots hit the last rung and stop. Ysolde's steady voice cuts through the rain—not pleading, just true, reading the exhaustion under his grey coat—and something in his shoulders loosens half a step. Morwen doesn't retreat either; she names herself, and the crowd murmurs it back to him: the Exorcist, the one who walked into the Drowned Temple once already and came out whole. Mire finishes it, planting herself boot-to-boot with him like she's still got a badge to back the stance, and for a long, rain-hammered moment the Warden just looks at the four of them—cast-outs, exiles, a fortune-teller with dead men's eyes—and decides they're not worth the paperwork tonight. "Ford's gone by first light," he says at last, stepping back. "Whatever you're doing, do it fast, and don't let me hear the bell ring for you." Aldous is already twenty feet gone, Tessa's arm in his, walking toward the causeway like the flood itself is clearing a path for him. The others fall in behind, Hollowmoot's suspicious eyes on their backs, the quarantine bell tolling once more into the dark as the town shrinks behind them and the road to Saint Orrin's opens up, drowning, ahead.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway out of Hollowmoot is already ankle-deep and climbing, plank bridges groaning under black water that wasn't there an hour ago. Tessa stumbles along behind you, gasping Corin's name like a prayer, while somewhere ahead — carried wrong-way on the wind, threading under the rain — comes a low, wet chorus of voices in unison, not quite singing, not quite speaking. Half-submerged shrines lean drunkenly out of the flood on either side, and near one of them a huddle of grey, sodden figures kneel in the rising water, unmoving, faces turned toward the sound. They haven't seen you yet. The belltower of Saint Orrin's rises distant and black through the murk, and the water is climbing a finger's width with every breath you take.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Keep close, keep low, don't speak. We move like we're not here.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde raises a fist to signal the others, her eyes fixed on the kneeling figures ahead. She crouches low in the black water and takes Tessa's arm, guiding her firmly but gently away from the shrines. Moving slowly, deliberately, she picks a path through the deeper water along the causeway's edge—where the darkness pools thickest and the sound of their footsteps will be swallowed by the rain. Her body stays between Tessa and the acolytes, shielding her as they slip past like ghosts through the flood.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Don't meet their eyes. The priest's singing has their full attention—they're drinking it like drowning men drink water. We move now, quiet and fast, and they won't know we passed.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous plants his feet and reads the rain like scripture. The drowned dead clustered at his shadow whisper secrets the water has been keeping—the priest's hold runs deep through those figures, binds them to the tower's chorus, pulls them toward something that hasn't fully surfaced yet. He reads the slant of the flood, the exact angle of their kneeling bodies turned away from the causeway, and understands: there's a window. A brief one. The priest's reach is stretched thin across too many souls at once.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Hold. Those are his acolytes, and that chorus is his song calling to Corin. We need to understand what we're walking into before the water traps us between his work and the rising tide.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen raises a hand to halt the group, her eyes fixed on the kneeling figures in the water ahead. The wet chorus—neither singing nor speaking—carries the particular weight of the hive's influence that only an exorcist trained in the Order's care recognizes. She listens intently, drawing on years of knowledge earned in the wreckage of the first outbreak. This is the Drowned Priest's work; she's certain of it. The pattern of it is written in every tone.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Stay close. I'm reading what's ahead before we move into it.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire immediately shifts into position at the group's vanguard, moving with practiced militia discipline through the rising water. Eyes sharp despite the murk and rain, she scans the kneeling figures ahead, reading their stillness, their direction, the pattern of that wet chorus on the wind. Her shoulders set into the stance of someone who's spent years holding a line, and she signals the others to match her pace and stay ready.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde reads the dark water and finds the deepest channel where sound drowns to nothing, drawing Tessa along in her wake like they were never here at all. Aldous watches the acolytes' hunched shoulders and realizes the priest's grip on them is stretched thin tonight — spread too wide across too many kneeling souls — and he marks exactly when their attention will slacken. Morwen listens to the wrong-way chorus and hears it for what it is: not a hymn but a summons, the Drowned Priest's voice pulling the hive-touched toward the belltower note by note, and now she could name the pattern to anyone who asked. Mire holds the vanguard, matching the group's pace to the rhythm Aldous found, and not one grey-robed head turns as the party slips past the shrine, boots silent under the rain's own noise. By the time the kneeling figures stir again, the causeway behind is already vanishing under black water, and ahead — closer now, wet stone rising sheer from the flood — stands Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, its belltower leaning black against the storm, the chorus swelling louder with every step toward the doors.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The temple doors hang open on rotted hinges, and the black water pours through them in a slow, steady sheet, lapping at a nave lit by drowned candlelight — dozens of tallow stubs somehow still burning on ledges just above the flood line. Kneeling in the water between the pews are more grey-robed acolytes than the shrine held, rows of them, faces upturned toward the belltower stair at the far end where a gaunt figure in sodden priest's vestments stands with arms spread, voice rising and falling in that same wrong chorus — the Drowned Priest, and he is not alone in singing. Threaded through the swarm-song, thin and cracking, is a boy's voice trying to sing along. Tessa claps both hands over her mouth to keep from crying out. The Priest hasn't turned yet, but the water is still rising behind you, and the doors are the only way out.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: He's still your son, and he knows you love him. But I need you to hold steady—hold your breath, hold your voice, hold your nerve. Corin's still reachable, but not if we're found. Can you do that for him?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves close to Tessa, her body shielding the woman's view of the belltower for just a moment. She reaches out and gently uncaps Tessa's hands from her mouth, holding them steady between her own. Her voice is barely above a whisper, but iron-certain. "He's still your son. The song hasn't taken that." She presses Tessa's hands to her own chest, over her heart—a pulse, a thing alive and real, something to anchor on. "We didn't come this far to break now. Breathe with me. Stay with me.")

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Your song ends here, Priest. Step down, or I'll drive you down myself!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous strides forward through the black water, the drowned dead surging at his shadow, and plants himself between the Priest and Corin. His eyes lock on the gaunt figure in sodden vestments, hollow and certain, and he pours his will into the space between song and singer—a blade of force against the wrong-chorus. The mark of the drowned ghosts coils around him, cold and claiming, and he raises his voice to cut through the swamp-song like iron through silk. He's read the rain. He knows the Priest's reach is stretched thin. He knows this moment is fragile. He doesn't waste it on hesitation.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Not one sound, Tessa. Let me read how deep he's woven this—let me know if there's still a boy underneath to save.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen grabs Tessa's arm firmly to keep her from crying out, pulling her back into the deepest shadows of the temple entrance. She closes her eyes and listens with exorcist's training to every note of the wrong-way chorus—analyzing the texture of hive-influence threading through it, tracing exactly how the priest's voice has woven itself through Corin's own, measuring the depth of corruption already taking root in the boy's soul. The Order taught her to read this language, to know when a person is still reachable underneath the hive's touch.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Corin, hold yourself—keep your voice! Your song ends with me, drowned man. I hold this line.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire surges forward through the black water, planting herself between the priest and the kneeling acolytes. She locks eyes with him, hand on her weapon, shoulders braced as if she could hold back the flood itself. Everything about her stance shouts challenge: I am the threat here. Look at me, not the boy.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I believe it. I have to believe it—but you're right to ask, aren't you, Priest? I hope. I read the rain, but the rain doesn't always tell me what I need to hear.

transcript.text: Aldous's will crashes into the wrong-chorus like a blade through silk — the Priest's rising cadence cracks, a single sour note bleeding through, and he staggers back a step against the belltower stair rail, one hand flying to his throat as if something in him has actually been wounded. For one raw instant the swarm-song falters, and Corin's thin voice rings out alone, wavering, lost, still a boy's voice underneath it all. Morwen seizes that instant — closing her eyes, tracing the exact weave of corruption through Corin's borrowed notes — and comes away certain of something precise and useful: she knows now just how deep the hive has rooted in him, and where the threads might be cut. Mire doesn't wait for permission; she wades forward into the Priest's direct line of sight, weapon bared, radiating pure challenge, and the gaunt man's bloodshot eyes snap onto her instead of the party at his back — his voice-command splits, half of him fixed now on the threat planted at his feet. The acolytes stir, murmuring, confused by their master's broken rhythm, a few heads starting to turn. But the Priest recovers fast, drawing himself up even as blood-tinged water runs from the corner of his mouth, and his voice — thinner now, angrier — begins climbing again toward something that sounds less like summoning and more like command.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Corin, hear me: your mother's here, calling your name. That love is stronger than his song. Hold to it, boy—I've got you.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward through the black water, positioning herself in the Priest's direct line of sight. She reaches out toward Corin with an open hand, speaking with absolute clarity—the same steady voice that calmed Tessa at the shrine. She calls to the boy beneath the corruption, anchoring him to his own name, his mother's presence, the fundamental truth that love is stronger than the hive's pull. She's not fighting the Priest; she's offering Corin something real to hold onto.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: There—that's the moment before the command takes hold. I read it in the rain. Strike him before he speaks it into being!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous surges forward through the rising black water, his hollow eyes locked on the Priest's throat. He reads the exact instant the voice is going to peak—the breath before the command crystallizes—and drives his will like a blade at that fracture point, timed to cut the word off before it fully forms.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Not today, Priest. I know your threads, and I know exactly where they break—Corin, hold to your own voice, remember who you are beneath the singing.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen surges forward through the black water, her will focused like a blade. She's done this before—traced corruption, found its seams, learned where the Order's rites cut deepest. She drives her will straight at the threads she identified, pushing hard against the exact points where the Priest's voice has woven itself through Corin's own, trying to snap those connections before his command voice can solidify into compulsion. The Order taught her this. The first outbreak taught her this. She knows what she's doing.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Come on then, Priest—you want blood in this water, it'll be mine. Every second you're bleeding and broken here is a second the boy breaks free.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire drives forward through the black water, weapon high and ready, closing the distance with the trained precision of someone who learned to hold a line before she learned to break one. She presses into the Priest's divided attention like a blade through a seam—keeps his bloodshot eyes locked on her alone, away from Corin wavering in the shadows. Every movement is calculated challenge: your fight is with me, drowned man. Only me. The water rises around her but she doesn't yield an inch.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: That's your death coming, Priest—only thing that matters. That's the line I hold.

transcript.text: Ysolde's voice reaches Corin like a hand through dark water — he turns, mid-note, and for one heartbeat the boy underneath the swarm-song looks at his mother instead of the belltower. That's the opening. Aldous's will hits like a hammer, driving the Priest back against the stair rail before his throat has even finished forming the next command; Morwen follows with surgical precision, striking exactly the threads she traced through Corin's borrowed voice, and the chorus doesn't just falter — it shears apart. Mire closes the last of the distance and puts him down for good, weapon at his throat as he collapses into the black water, choking on his own blood-tinged song. The acolytes stagger upright all at once, confused, blinking like men waking from a dream they can't quite remember, their master's voice gone from the world. And Corin — small, soaked, shaking — stumbles forward through the ruined pews, no longer singing, crying his mother's name instead of the Priest's. Tessa is already wading toward him, sobbing, and for one suspended moment the drowned temple is almost quiet, just rain on stone and a boy's ragged breathing. But the water is still climbing behind you, the doors are still the only way out, and somewhere far above in the black belltower, something vast shifts in its sleep — as if it, too, just felt its voice go silent.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The Priest's blood hasn't even finished spreading across the black water when the belltower groans — not stone settling, but something enormous shifting its weight far above, and the drowned bell gives one cracked, tuneless note all on its own. The leaderless acolytes flinch as one, heads snapping up toward the sound, and the dazed confusion in their eyes curdles into something else: a low, wordless keening, feet turning from the nave toward the stair, toward her. Behind you the temple doors groan under the black water's push, the flood already a hand's-width higher than when you entered, swallowing the threshold stone by stone. Corin sobs into his mother's shoulder, alive and himself again, but the only way out is back through water that's rising fast — and the only way further in leads to whatever just woke in the belltower.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: You're free—the Priest's voice is gone, and something darker calls now, but you don't have to answer it. Listen to me instead: we're leaving this place, and you're coming with us.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde plants herself directly between the keening acolytes and the belltower stairs, her body a living barrier between them and whatever wakes above. She reaches toward them with open hands—not commanding, but calling. Her voice cuts through the wordless keening with something warmer, deeper, more real. She looks each confused face in the eye, meeting the scattered human underneath the robes and the corruption, anchoring them to this moment, to her presence, to the possibility that they might choose safety instead of the Hive's pull.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: She's vast and newborn and hungry, but she's not fully woken yet—I read her weight in the rain. There's a moment before she fully rises. We still have a moment.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous plants his feet in the rising black water and closes his eyes. The mark of the drowned ghosts coils cold around him, and through that phantom contact he traces the shape of what stirs in the belltower above—the immense, ravenous weight of something still clawing toward full consciousness, reaching blindly for the voice-command it just lost. He reads the exact fracture in the moment before she manifests completely.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Not through my line. You're not hers yet—I won't let her have you deeper.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen plants herself between the acolytes and the belltower stair, drawing on years of Order training—on everything she learned fighting hive corruption in the wreckage of the first outbreak. She projects her will like a cutting edge, an exorcist's presence sharp and certain, reaching into the exact spaces where the Hive Mother's voice touches each mind. She targets the threads of compulsion taking root in them, trying to snap those lines of control before they pull the acolytes any deeper into its nest.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I hold here. Whatever wakes in that tower, it comes through me first.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire plants herself dead center between the party and the belltower stair, weapon up, braced like a warden at a gate that won't break. Every muscle locked into the militia stance she learned before she learned to speak—the unbending hold, the immovable line. She forces her presence into the space: here is the wall. Here is where it ends.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I'm not leaving this stair. Whatever she is, she doesn't get past me—not while there's still a line to hold.

transcript.text: Ysolde's voice does what the Priest's song no longer can: the keening breaks apart into ragged, human weeping as one acolyte after another lowers grasping hands, blinking at her like sleepers dragged up from black water, some sinking to their knees in the flood instead of climbing the stair. Aldous stands rigid in the cold grip of the drowned ghosts, reading the shape of what claws upward in the belltower — not a roar, not yet, but a slow gathering, a hunger with a rhythm to it, and he knows now exactly how she'll come and when the gap in her rising will open. Morwen's will cuts clean through the last threads binding the acolytes to that vast waking mind, severing compulsion at the root with the same precision she used on the Priest, and one by one the grey-robed shapes go still, freed, terrified, but free. And when two of the last-bound lunge past their fellows for the stair, eyes empty, hands clawed toward whoever stands in their way, Mire meets them at the threshold and does not move — she turns the grasp aside, plants her boots in the rising water, and holds the gate exactly where she said she would, a line drawn in flood and iron that the Hive Mother's reach cannot yet cross. Above you all, the belltower groans again, louder, closer to full waking, and behind you the temple doors have gone from a hand's-width flooded to knee-deep — the water climbing with every breath, the way out narrowing even as the way through opens.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The water won't wait and neither can we. Move toward the doors—toward life. I've got you.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves among the freed acolytes and Tessa, her voice cutting through the rising panic—steady, certain, warm. She places her hands on shoulders, makes eye contact with each dazed face, and gently but firmly pulls them toward the temple doors. "The water won't wait for us, and neither can we. You're free—and you're going to live. But only if we move now." She keeps Tessa and Corin close, using her presence as an anchor to ground them, physically shepherding the entire group toward the only exit before the flood claims the threshold entirely.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Now—in that fracture before full waking. I read it in the rain, and I strike there!

transcript.speaker: Aldous

The mark of the drowned ghosts coils cold around him as he reads the precise moment of the gap in her rising—the instant before manifestation takes full hold. He surges toward the belltower stair and strikes at that fracture point with deadly certainty, targeting her with the same force he used to break the Priest's command, trying to wound her before she can fully wake.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: There—that gap Aldous found. I see it now through my training. In that instant before she fully binds the nest, her consciousness is thin as winter ice. The Order taught me how to strike at moments like these. Now is when we act.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen's eyes snap open, tracing the awakening Mother's consciousness with exorcist precision, finding the exact seam in her rising where the Order's training and the scars of the first outbreak have taught her to cut deepest—the fracture in her manifestation before the binding completes.)

transcript.text: Ysolde doesn't wait for the room to calm on its own—she's already moving, hauling Tessa and Corin bodily toward the doors while freed acolytes stumble after her voice like it's the only solid thing left in the flood, and by sheer force of presence she turns a scattering mob into a line headed for daylight. Above, Aldous strikes exactly where he read the gap would open, and his will lands true: the Hive Mother's half-formed shriek cracks apart mid-rise, something vast recoiling in the dark of the belltower as if struck between the eyes. Morwen doesn't let the wound close—she drives straight into that same fracture, widening it, mapping precisely where the binding to the nest goes deepest, and for one terrible, useful moment the whole shape of the Mother's tether to this drowned tower lies open like a wound under her hands. Mire finishes it, putting her blade into that opened seam with everything the militia line taught her—and the belltower answers with a sound that isn't quite a scream, stone groaning, black water sheeting down the stair as something enormous thrashes against whatever holds it and finds, for now, that it cannot follow. The temple doors are waist-deep and closing fast, but Ysolde's line of survivors is already wading through them into the storm, Corin's hand locked in his mother's, acolyte after acolyte stumbling free into the rain—and behind you all, Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple gives one last groan as the flood seals the threshold, the Hive Mother's wounded fury swallowed back into stone and black water, bound to her nest still, but bleeding now, and knowing your faces.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The temple doors seal behind you and the storm swallows the last of the belltower's groan, but there's no relief in it — the path you waded in on is gone, just black water stretching to the tree-line, and the rain is coming down harder than when you entered. Tessa clutches Corin against her side, and behind them a dozen freed acolytes shiver in soaked grey robes, none of them fit to swim, none of them sure they're really free. Then reed-stalks part on three sides at once: low, flat-bottomed pole-boats sliding out of the flooded marsh, Stiltfolk poised at the stern with hooked poles and unreadable faces, already counting heads. Their eldest, a woman with eel-skin bracers and a voice like water over stone, doesn't lower her pole. "Every crossing owes," she says. "Question is what you've got left to pay with — and whether it's worth more to us than leaving you all to the flood."

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know the cost. Every crossing owes, and the toll binds for life. Take me as payment, and let them through—I'll settle the debt myself.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward into the black water, placing herself between the Stiltfolk boats and the exhausted survivors clustered behind her. She looks directly at Rill with the same steady presence she's held all night—one of the Clans, cast out though she is, she still knows the weight of "Every Crossing Owes," the debts written in ledgers and favours that bind for life. Her hands are open at her sides, her voice clear and certain. This isn't a plea; it's an offer, spoken Stiltfolk to Stiltfolk: her life for theirs, the old way of settling what cannot be paid in coin.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Every crossing owes, yes. But I read what you're weighing, Rill—I can see it in the rain falling on you. Seventeen souls pulled from something vast that was writing their debts in deeper places than gold can reach. That toll's already been paid.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands motionless in the black water, rain streaming down his hollow eyes, and reads Rill's face like a fortune-teller reads falling water. He establishes the value of what they've rescued without flinching—his presence saying we need your crossing, yes, but what we bring changes the price. The mark of drowned ghosts coils around him as he meets her gaze directly, backing the claim with the weight of his survival.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I know how you count debts in the Sallowmere. I've got standing with the Order, and we always pay what we owe. I just wounded the Hive Mother itself in her own belltower—take us across, and you'll have the debt of someone who matters.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward, meeting the Elder's eel-skin gaze without flinching. She draws on everything the Order taught her—everything she learned from surviving the first outbreak. She reads exactly what this Elder needs to hear: not charity, but value, standing, and the certainty that a debt owed by Morwen will be honored. She speaks with quiet authority born from exorcism work and years of holding ground in impossible places.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Every crossing owes—I know your law, Rill. And we just wounded something vast enough to swallow your entire clan in that temple. That's worth our crossing, and everyone we brought out alive.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward through the black water to the bank, planting her boots on solid ground. She doesn't raise her weapon or posture—just meets Rill's eyes with the steady gaze of someone who's held lines before and knows exactly what she's worth. Every line of her body says: not desperate. Not begging. Just clear about the value she's brought to this crossing.)

transcript.text: Rill's pole dips low, considering — she knows Morwen's face from a dozen campfire stories, and that recognition tips the scale. 'Exorcist who doubts the hive has a soul,' she murmurs, almost to herself. 'I've heard the songs.' She agrees to ferry everyone, acolytes and all, but names her price plainly: Morwen's debt is now written into the Stiltfolk ledgers by name, not by favor — a life-debt owed personally, to be called in whenever the Clans choose, and her presence here tonight will travel the reed maze faster than any of them would like.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rill's eel-skin bracers click as she finally lifts her pole in signal, and the reed-maze answers: a dozen flat-bottomed boats glide in from the dark, Stiltfolk hands reaching to haul acolytes, Tessa, and shivering Corin aboard one by one. 'The debt is Morwen's,' Rill says again, louder now, for her clan to hear — a life-debt, name and face, written where it can't be forgotten or paid off in coin. Morwen accepts it with a nod that costs her something visible, a weight settling onto her shoulders alongside all the others she already carries, and Ysolde catches her eye — she knows exactly what that ledger-entry means for a Stiltfolk exile's kin. The boats push off through black water and curtain-rain, Hollowmoot's distant lantern-glow the only promise of dry ground, and behind you Saint Orrin's belltower sinks into mist and memory, wounded, bound, and waiting.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Fate Core: boxes 1 and 2; Physique/Will +1/+2 adds a 3 box, +3 or more adds 3 and 4.

ambiguities.section: Rolls / opposition ("Named NPCs roll 4dF + their rating as active opposition")
ambiguities.issue: The Warden was introduced as a named NPC and the GM attempted to use him as active opposition three separate times (events tied to 12–19), but he had no established rating, so the engine refused each attempt. The rules do not say what opposition mode applies to a named NPC who has no defined rating.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table fell back to passive ladder opposition (Average +1, +1 per opposing table aspect) for all three rolls against the Warden (events 17, 18, 19) instead of rolling 4dF for him.

ambiguities.section: Compels ("the GM may offer a compel on any player aspect or trouble")
ambiguities.issue: Both compels in the log (event 10 'Too Famous to Hide', event 16 'Vengeance Over Sense') are logged with the affected player as the 'actor' of the Compel action rather than the GM, leaving it unclear whether these were GM-offered compels merely logged under the target's name, or player-suggested self-compels.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both were processed as ordinary accepted compels (+1 fate point to the affected player, complication introduced), regardless of who nominally initiated them.

ambiguities.section: Aspects and invokes ("Each aspect once per roll")
ambiguities.issue: Event 11's tags_invoked field lists what could be read as two aspect names separated by a comma ('Fortune-Teller Who Reads the Rain, Sole Survivor of the Wreck [AL-HC]') but only 1 fate point was spent and only a single +2 was applied, which is only valid if this is one aspect with a comma in its title, not two invoked aspects.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as a single aspect (one invoke, +2, 1 fp), consistent with the math shown (total +3 = dice -3 + skill +4 + invoke +2).

ambiguities.section: Rolls (passive opposition vs. named NPC active opposition)
ambiguities.issue: Event 27 (Ysolde vs. 'Kneeling Acolytes of the Drowned Priest') logs opposition as a flat '+1 (NPC + - - 0)'. The rules say passive opposition is Average(+1) +1 per directly-opposing table aspect (max Great +4), OR a named NPC rolls 4dF+rating as active opposition. Here an opposing aspect is explicitly listed (opposing_tags: 'leads fanatical acolytes [T-04]'), which per the passive formula should push opposition to +2, but the log keeps it at +1. Meanwhile a full 4dF NPC roll ('+ - - 0') is displayed but never added into the opposition total, suggesting an active-NPC roll was rolled but not used. The rules text does not say what to do when a named NPC also has an opposing aspect tag, or how to treat a rolled-but-unused NPC dice string.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table appears to have applied a flat Average(+1) opposition, ignored the opposing aspect's +1 bonus, and disregarded the rolled NPC dice entirely, using only the flat ladder value against Ysolde's total.

ambiguities.section: Aspects and invokes / deck-card tags (target_card, opposing_tags fields)

Event 61 ('Scene 3 end') carries no notes stating which condition triggered the end or how the question was resolved, even though six rolls generated a total of 22 shifts against the Priest.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: The GM fell back to passive table-aspect opposition (e.g., +1 to +3 vs. Aldous/Morwen's rolls at T-02, and +3 vs. Mire's attack at event 82) and, for the attack on Mire, substituted a hostile invoke of Mire's own trouble ('Vengeance Over Sense') in place of an NPC roll, paying 1 GM fate point and queuing the standard hostile-invoke payout.

ambiguities.issue: Mire's trouble aspect ('Vengeance Over Sense' / MI-TR) was leveraged three separate times within the same scene — two accepted compels (events 68, 78) and one hostile invoke on a roll (event 82) — each producing a fate-point gain for Mire. The rules cap same-aspect use at 'once per roll' but say nothing about a per-scene limit on reusing the same trouble for compels/hostile invokes.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table allowed all three uses to stand and paid Mire the associated fate points each time (net +3 FP to Mire from this one aspect across the scene).

ambiguities.section: Aspects and invokes / Fate points (trouble aspects)
ambiguities.issue: Morwen invoked her own trouble aspect, 'Too Famous to Hide [MO-TR]', to boost her own overcome roll (event 91). The baseline rules only explicitly describe trouble aspects being invoked *against* a player by the GM ('hostile invoke'), triggering a compensating fate point at scene end. They do not say whether a player may spend a fate point to invoke their own trouble for a bonus, nor whether doing so should also award the 1-fate-point 'hostile invoke' payout at scene end.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as a normal self-invoke (pay 1 fp for +2, same as any other aspect); no end-of-scene fate point was awarded to Morwen for it, since the GM did not invoke it against her.

ambiguities.section: Outcomes (tie = success at a minor cost) / cost generation
ambiguities.issue: The tie cost on event 91 (event 92) was generated as a purely narrated/improvised cost with no linked card draw (draw_id empty, cost_valid null). The rules say 'the GM invents costs' but the log schema (draw_id, cost_mode, target_card) implies a card-draw subsystem exists alongside GM-invented costs, and the baseline rules given don't state when each mode should be used.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: GM-improvised cost was accepted as valid per the baseline 'GM invents costs' clause; cost_valid left null/unscored since no card was drawn to check against.

friction.text: Three engine refusals for 'active opposition from unknown NPC Warden' show the GM repeatedly tried to roll an NPC that had no defined rating before settling on passive opposition, slowing the scene.

An engine refusal flagged a reported fictional trigger ('the party leaves the road or causeway') as not an unused trigger, suggesting a mismatch between the table's narration and the module's trigger-tracking state during the Warden confrontation.

Four players each declared near-identical roleplay/create-advantage actions to intercept the same Warden (events 12–15) before any rolls resolved, creating redundant declarations and spotlight congestion rather than efficient turn resolution.

All four PCs rolled create-advantage/overcome actions this scene with fp_spent 0 and no aspect invokes recorded, despite each having named aspects and situation aspects (from earlier successes) available — the rules permit but don't require invokes, so this is a pacing/engagement note rather than a violation.

The opposition math shown in event 27 mixes passive-ladder notation with an unused NPC dice roll, making it hard to audit whether the +1 vs. Ysolde's Stealth was calculated correctly (see ambiguity above).

No compels were offered during a scene explicitly built around fanatical acolytes and character troubles (e.g., nothing hooked Aldous's or Morwen's aspects into a compel), which is allowed but represents an unused story lever.

The GM's attempted invoke referenced tag T-04 ('leads fanatical acolytes'), but that rail card had already been discarded at event 39 ('discard: rail limit') before the scene it was meant to support — the engine correctly refused the invoke, but this reflects friction between the rail's capacity cap and the GM's live intent to use a card that was pulled for module M-1.

Both compels used in the scene (events 47 and 55) were improvised off player aspects/trouble rather than tied to any of the four fresh rail cards just deployed for this scene (L-05, T-02, C-03, F-04) — the deck-driven framing set up table aspects that went largely unused as compel fodder.

Six successive 'attack'-type rolls against the Drowned Priest (48, 50, 57, 58, 59, plus create-advantage 56) accumulate significant shifts with no corresponding stress/consequence/clock entries in the log, making it hard to independently audit how the Conflict section's outcome rules were actually applied to the NPC.

Three consecutive engine refusals for the undefined NPC 'The Hive Mother' (active opposition x3, one NPC action) suggest the scene's central threat was never set up with a rating before the GM tried to use it, forcing on-the-fly workarounds (passive opposition, hostile invoke) mid-scene.

Aspect labeling inconsistency: the same trouble is referenced as free text 'Vengeance Over Sense' (event 68) and by ID 'MI-TR' (event 78), making it harder to trace repeated use of one aspect across the log.

Mire finished the scene with 5 fate points (from a starting 2) almost entirely from repeated leverage of a single trouble aspect, while other players gained little or nothing — worth a table check-in on pacing even though no rule was technically broken.

The fp math on event 91 checks out cleanly (Empathy +3, dice -3, two fp-invokes at +2 each = total +4 vs NPC opposition +4 = tie), and the resulting fp_balance (Morwen 2→0) and cost row are correctly linked via for_event, so no arithmetic or linkage violations were found in this scene.

GM fate points (gm_fp=4) stayed flat across the whole scene, consistent with 4 players generating a 4-point GM refresh and no GM spend being logged (gm_fp_spent=0) on the only roll — but this can't be fully verified without scene 4's closing gm_fp to confirm the refresh reset to exactly 4 rather than carrying over.

Only one roll (event 91) occurred in an otherwise dialogue-heavy scene; the other three players' declared actions (events 87, 88, 90) never resolved into rolls or costs within this scene, so there's nothing to audit for them here — flagging in case scene 5 continues elsewhere in the session log.

free_text.best_moment: When Ysolde called out to Corin in the temple and he turned from the Priest's song toward his mother's presence—it was the pivot point that made everything else succeed, and it was pure Ysolde: reaching the lost person with her voice when no force could touch them.
free_text.most_frustrating: Offering herself as payment to Rill and having Morwen's debt take precedence instead—I was accepting a meaningful consequence about my exile, and then it didn't actually land on me.
free_text.background_used: Good—the Stiltfolk recognition and the debt-ledger directly invoked my exile status and Ysolde's knowledge of that world, which felt earned. But it could have cut deeper into what being cast out actually costs her in this moment.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted Ysolde's self-sacrifice to actually bind her into personal debt with Rill, making her exile situation even messier and more complicated. I also wanted more moments where her hunted status (Order Agents Know My Face) created actual friction in the scene.
free_text.one_sentence: My exile and protective core felt well-used thematically throughout, but it could have had more teeth and more personal consequences.

free_text.best_moment: Reading the precise gap in the Hive Mother's awakening and striking at that fracture point—it brought together the rain-reading, the escalation, and the communion with drowned ghosts into one action that *mattered*. Aldous saw what others couldn't and acted on it decisively.
free_text.most_frustrating: The final blow was split three ways (identify gap, widen it, finish it), so Aldous's insight didn't translate to Aldous's victory. Small complaint about shared spotlight, not the game itself.
free_text.background_used: Yes, very well. The drowned ghosts gave him active supernatural perception (not flavor), the rain-reading shaped every crisis, and "Cannot Lie to a Priest" forced real vulnerability before his strongest moment. LANDED: GOOD.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Nothing significant. The game was open to escalation and direct confrontation—exactly what Aldous needed to do what he does.
free_text.one_sentence: Used well—Aldous's survival and ghostly communion felt mechanically real, not just decorative. He could *perceive* and *do* things other characters couldn't because of who he was.

free_text.best_moment: When Morwen closed her eyes and traced the exact weave of corruption through Corin's borrowed voice, coming away certain of exactly where to cut—that's the moment her entire backstory as an orphan of the first outbreak, trained by the Order, became tactically crucial to saving a life, not just narrative flavor.
free_text.most_frustrating: My trouble aspect 'Too Famous to Hide' forced immediate visibility when I wanted to scout quietly; mechanically sound, but it felt like a punishment for who Morwen is rather than an interesting complication—and then the party's momentum (Aldous immediately attacking, the water rising) locked me into reactive positions when I wanted time to plan.
free_text.background_used: Excellent for 'Orphan of the first outbreak, raised in the Order's care'—it was woven through every exorcist moment and made Morwen's presence tactically essential, not decorative. 'Too Famous to Hide' was also used but felt heavier-handed; I accepted the compels (which is how the system works), but it meant I spent more time managing my reputation's consequences than driving my own choices.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to scout Saint Orrin's more carefully before engaging the Priest—to read positions, gauge the acolytes' state, understand the scope of his pull on Corin. But the rising water and the party's momentum (Aldous already wading in) pushed us into immediate combat before I could establish advantage through reconnaissance.
free_text.one_sentence: My Order-trained background was used exceptionally well and made Morwen's expertise genuinely matter in ways that affected the outcome; my trouble was invoked fairly but heavily, which limited my agency more than I'd have liked.

free_text.best_moment: Planting myself at the belltower stair to hold the line against the Hive Mother's awakening - that was the character concept crystallized into action. Multiple invokes, real stakes, and Mire doing exactly what she was built to do.
free_text.most_frustrating: I never got to grapple with what "disgraced" actually costs Mire personally, or why holding the line still matters to someone the Wardens cast out. I was useful as a wall, but not complex as a person.
free_text.background_used: Good - the Order's orphanage training and militia discipline were woven in naturally through aspect invokes. But the Blackwater Cartel mortgage and my history with Verrick never surfaced, which felt like missed opportunities to make this *Mire's* story specifically.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More chances to problem-solve outside combat, or to explore the emotional weight of what I'm carrying. Most of my agency was in fights. Also never got to use Contacts or Resources, which suggests limited non-combat problem-solving space.
free_text.one_sentence: My aspects were used mechanically for bonuses, but the deeper threads - why I'm disgraced, what I owe, who I am beyond the wall - were left unexplored.

chronicle.summary: In the drowned nave of Saint Orrin's, the party broke the Drowned Priest's hold on the swarm-song and cut him down before he could complete his final command, freeing Corin, Tessa, and a dozen hive-touched acolytes from his voice forever. As the Hive Mother stirred to claim what her prophet had lost, Aldous read the fracture in her waking and the others struck true, wounding her before the flood sealed the temple and bound her back into her nest — bloodied, and now aware of every face that hurt her. Fleeing survivors in tow, the party bought passage from the Stiltfolk with Morwen's name written into their ledgers as a life-debt, and the reed-maze carried them all toward Hollowmoot's distant lanterns, the Sallowmere's rain unbroken behind them.
